City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022
  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 7, 2022

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Menchaca
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Menchaca,
  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PROCLAMATION FOR LGBTQ+ PRIDE MONTH
  B. JUNETEENTH DAY

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-40 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-40 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-40 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 17, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022  2
   2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of May 17, 2022.

  3. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 26, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2022-2023

  California Government Code Section 53646 requires the annual review of the
  City’s Investment Policy at a regular meeting of the City Council. The
  requirement for an annual policy is also stated in the City’s Fiscal Sustainability
  Policy (adopted April 2019 in the interest of fiscal accountability). The
  Investment Policy is reviewed and adopted annually by the City Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 22-30 adopting
  2022-2023 Statement of Investment Policy.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 22-29 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 300 BLOCK OF PASQUAL AVENUE

  The request for a temporary street closure is to host an Independence Day
  Celebration on Monday, July 4, 2022 on the 300 block of Pasqual Avenue
  between Sycamore Drive to the end of the cul-de-sac. The block party will be
  held from 6:00 P.M. to 10:00 P.M.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-29 authorizing
  closure on Pasqual Avenue between Sycamore Drive to the end of the cul-de-
  sac from 6:00 P.M. to 10:00 P.M. on Monday, July 4, 2022.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022  3
   F. REQUEST FOR ANNUAL RATE REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENTS FOR STREET
  SWEEPING SERVICE AND SOLID WASTE SERVICE WITH ATHENS SERVICES

  In accordance with the Sixth Amendment dated July 6, 2021, Athens Services
  has submitted two rate reviews for City Council’s approval to adjust the rates
  for street sweeping and solid waste services with Consumer Price Indices
  increases effective July 1, 2022.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the annual rate adjustments
  proposed by Athens Services for its services not to exceed the attached rate
  schedules (see Exhibit A and B in staff report), effective July 1, 2022.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF PROPOSED OPERATING BUDGET, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM, FEE SCHEDULE, POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY
  SCHEDULE, AND APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  Select the links below to access the attachments.

  Attachment A  Attachment B  Attachment C
  Attachment D  Attachment E  Attachment F

  The City Council will hold a Public Hearing to consider adoption of the
  Proposed Operating Budget, Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), Fee Schedule,
  Position Classification and Salary Schedule, and Appropriations Limit for Fiscal
  Year 2022-2023. The General Fund operating budget is balanced with a slight
  surplus of $366,610. Projected revenues for all City funds is $82,235,872.
  Proposed expenditures for all City funds is $81,406,839. The proposed new
  funding for CIP is $11,432,396, which would provide resources for 14 CIP
  projects.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the
  Proposed 2022-23 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets, Fee
  Schedule, Compensation Schedule and Appropriations Limit, and after
  receiving comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022  4
   1. Resolution No. 22-33 adopting the City of San Gabriel Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023 Operating Budget
  2. Resolution No. 22-32 adopting the 2022-2023 Capital Improvement
  Program Budget
  3. Resolution No. 22-31 adopting the Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023
  4. Resolution No. 22-38 adopting the amended authorized schedule of
  compensation and benefits for Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  5. Resolution No. 22-37 establishing the City of San Gabriel’s appropriation
  limit for the Fiscal Year 2022-23

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION REGARDING SAN GABRIEL’S TRANSIT PROGRAM

  The City Council approved an updated agreement with First Transit for an
  expanded transit program to include Dial-A-Ride or paratransit, and microtransit
  services. Staff is presenting the following information for City Council discussion
  and approval, including: possible names for the service, parameters for the
  transit program and timeline for the system kickoff.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the information presented and:
  1. Approve the name of San Gabriel’s new transit system; and
  2. Discuss and approve the transit parameters presented.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTIONS RELATING TO THE CALLING OF SAN
  GABRIEL’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 8,
  2022

  This item calls the General Municipal Election for November 8, 2022, for the
  election of three Members of the City Council, City Clerk, and City Treasurer;
  requests consolidation with the Statewide General Election, and sets regulations
  for candidate statements. In accordance with Section 1301 of the California
  Elections Code, San Gabriel’s General Municipal Elections are held on the first
  Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year. The
  cost of holding the election is estimated at $105,000.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 22-34 calling for the holding of a General Municipal
  Election on Tuesday, November 8, 2022.
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 22-35 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to consolidate, administer, manage and oversee the
  Election.
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 22-36 establishing regulations for candidate
  statements.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING A PAST PROPOSAL FROM THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT TO PROVIDE FIRE SERVICES TO THE CITY OF
  SAN GABRIEL

  In 2018, in order to consider alternatives to maintaining the City’s own fire
  department, a proposal was requested from the Los Angeles County Fire
  Department for the cost to provide fire services to the City. The costs of the
  proposal was updated in 2019 but discussion on whether to consider a move to
  consolidating with the County of Los Angeles was put on hold due to the City’s
  financial condition at that time, and then the COVID-19 pandemic. An updated
  cost proposal was recently requested and received, the results of which indicate
  that changing the City’s services to Los Angeles County does not make sense at
  this time. Staff will present details of the proposal and the cost analysis, with a
  recommendation to end discussions with the County at this time.
  (PRESENTATION)

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to discontinue discussions
  with LA County at this time.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 7, 2022  6
   Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – POTENTIAL/PENDING LITIGATION
  (Government Code §54956.9[d][2])
  (one potential case)

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 21, 2022 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF JUNE 7, 2022

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCI L

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ding called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:47
  P.M. on Tuesday, June 7, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Menchaca.

  RO LL CALL
  Council Members Present:  Denise Menchaca, Carina Rivera, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  John R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief

I  City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias,  Finance  Director  William  Kaholokula,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Special City Council Meetings of May 26, 2022, and June 6, 2022, same item:

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias, Labor Relations Counsel Steve Filarsky.

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officers'
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighters'
  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented Employees.

I  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that no reportable action was taken.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINU TES  Page 1 of 6  June 7, 2022
   Hearing no objection, Mayor Ding stated the agenda order was approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PROCLAMATION FOR LGBTQ+ PRIDE MONTH

  Mayor Ding made the presentation and San Gabriel LGBTQ+ Center Board
  Member Vicky Mitchell accepted the proclamation.

I  B. JUNETEENTH DAY

  Mayor Ding made the presentation and Human Equity, Access, and Relations
  (HEAR) Commission Chair Chasity Jennings-Nunez accepted the proclamation .

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, commented on the fire hazard posed by dead trees on
  private property in the City and requested that the City take action.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, commented on the adoption of Resolution No. 20 -
  31 which led to the establishment of the HEAR Commission; and commented on HEAR
  Commission accomplishments and projects, and on work still to be done to advance
  diversity.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor

I  Harrington, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-40 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY'S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY FOR
  CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-40 regard ing the use of
  teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following :

I  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 17, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of May 17, 2022.
  3. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 26, 2022.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved May 5, 2022, May 12, 2022, and May 20, 2022, Reg isters
  of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING M INU TES  Page 2 of 6  June 7, 2022
   D. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2022-2023

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-30 adopting the 2022-2023
  Statement of Investment Policy.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 22-29 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY STREET
  CLOSURE ON THE 300 BLOCK OF PASQUAL AVENUE

I  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-29 authorizing closure on Pasqual
  Avenue, between Sycamore Drive to the end of the cul-de-sac, from 6:00 P.M. to
  10:00 P.M . on Monday, July 4, 2022.

  F. REQUEST FOR ANNUAL RATE REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENTS FOR STREET
  SWEEPING SERVICE AND SOLID WASTE SERVICE WITH ATHENS SERVICES

  The City Council approved the annual rate adjustments proposed by Athens
  Services for its services, not to exceed the rate schedules included in the staff
  report, effective July 1, 2022.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF PROPOSED OPERATING BUDGET, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM, FEE SCHEDULE, POSITION CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY
  SCHEDULE, AND APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  Mayor Ding opened the public hearing.

I  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included whether a vacancy factor was accounted for in the
  number for projected tax revenue for Fiscal Year 2022-23; conservative
  methodology for property-tax projections; and planning for a vacancy factor for
  major taxpayers.

  There was no public comment.

  Mayor Ding closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included Measure SG revenues realized and projected, and changes in
  state sales tax projected revenue.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Rivera, to adopt the following:

  1. Resolution No. 22-33 adopting the City of San Gabriel Fiscal Year 2022-2023

I  Operating Budget.
  2. Resolution No. 22-32 adopting the 2022-2023 Capital Improvement Program
  Budget.
  3. Resolution No. 22-31 adopting the Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 .
  4. Resolution No. 22-38 adopting the amended authorized schedule of
  compensation and benefits for Fiscal Year 2022-2023.
  5. Resolution No. 22-37 establishing the City of San Gabriel's appropriation limit
  for Fiscal Year 2022-23

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  June 7, 2022
   Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU , HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  AB STAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

I  A. DISCUSSION REGARDING SAN GABRIEL'S TRANSIT PROGRAM

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  Discussion included having a virtual suggestion box to assess additional rider
  needs; cost impact for extended hours on certain days; having a higher weekend
  rate; current ridership numbers; timeline for implementation of the new transit
  program; service for special events; child-safety seats to be provided by riders;
  using data from ridership and a virtual suggestion box to consider future
  adjustments on the number of vehicles or prices; cancellation timeframe and fees;
  ride payment options; logo design; paid advertisements on the vehicles; and
  promotion of the new program.

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, stated her preference for the name of the program,
  expressed safety concerns about young riders, and inquired about gas price impact
  on costs.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

I  A. CON SIDERATION OF RESOLUTIONS RELATING TO THE CALLING OF SAN
  GABRIEL'S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 8,
  2022

  Chief City Clerk Clark made the presentation .

  There was no public comment.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Rivera, to:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 22 -34 calling for the holding of a General Mun icipal
  Election on Tuesday, November 8, 2022.
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 22 -35 requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to consolidate, administer, manage and oversee the
  Election.
  3. Adopt Resolut ion  No.  22-36  establishing  regulations  for  candidate

I  statements.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINU TES  Page 4 of 6  Ju ne 7, 2022
   Mayor Ding recessed the meeting at 8:25 P.M. and reconvened at 8:37 P.M . with all
  Council Members present.

  B. DISCUSSION REGARDING A PAST PROPOSAL FROM THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT TO PROVIDE FIRE SERVICES TO THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL

  City Manager Lazzaretto and Fire Chief Wallace made the presentation.

I  Discussion included Unfunded Accrued Liability (UAL) for both City and County
  models over time; the San Gabriel Fire Fighters' Association (FFA) voted
  overwhelmingly to stay as the San Gabriel Fire Department (SGFD); location, time
  period, and customer service level for fire inspection permits under the County
  model; time interval to reconsider service -model options; and the SGFD has better
  response times than the County.

  There was no public comment.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to discontinue discussions
  with LA County for fire services at this time.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto gained consensus from the City Council that unless pressing
  matters arise, the July 5, 2022, regular City Council meeting would be cancelled .

I  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Wu reported on a Memorial Day event hosted by the City of
  Rosemead and requested agendizing an item for a City War Memorial; and reported
  on the Asian World Film Festival.

  Council Member Menchaca announced that Florence Lin, San Gabriel's 2022
  Outstanding Older American, was given a congressional award for Woman of the Year
  by Congresswoman Judy Chu; and suggested that since the Community Services
  Commission is already working on plans for a War Memorial, that process be allowed
  to continue.

  Council Member Rivera reported on attend ing the Woman of the Year event hosted
  by Congresswoman Chu, and agreed with Council Member Wu that a memorial for
  veterans is needed.

  Mayor Ding commended Florence Lin on her award; reported on the Asian Film

I  Festival; and announced a Thanks U.S.A. event on June 25, 2022, hosted by the San
  Gabriel Hope Lions Club, Hope Center, I-Ch inese Political Action Committee (!PAC),
  and Asian American Advocacy All iance (AAAA).

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  Mayor Ding recessed the meeting at 9:26 P.M. and reconvened in Closed Session at 9:37
  P.M. with all Council Members present.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  CITY COUNCI L REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 6  June 7, 2022
   A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - POTENTIAL/PENDING LITIGATION
  (Government Code §54956.9[d][2]) (one potential case)

  There was no reportable action.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 10:39 P.M.
